title: Capacity-aware admission control and geo-failover policy for variant rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Implement a capacity-aware admission control layer and geo-failover policy that sits in front of deployment rollouts (canaries, A/B, shadow). The feature ensures that: 1) new model variants are admitted only when per-region capacity and compatibility constraints are satisfied; 2) rollouts can soft-throttle and gracefully shed load to compatible fallback variants when a tier or region is saturated; and 3) automatic rollback triggers combine quality regressions and latency/cost SLO breaches. This ticket covers the design, prototype, integration with the routing policy compiler, and end-to-end tests.

Key behaviors to implement: admission bucketing based on available GPU slots and token-rate capacity; semantic compatibility scoring (op-level and response-shape checks) to determine acceptable fallback variants; soft-throttle admission (gradual increase with backpressure tokens) for canary phases; cross-region failover with prioritized tiers; and auto-rollback policy that requires both signal types (quality regressions from evals / user metrics and infrastructure SLO breaches) to reduce noisy rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces per-region capacity buckets and rejects canary traffic when projected queueing delay > 150ms for median requests
Soft-throttle ramp implemented: canary ramp increases from 0% to target over staged windows and honors backpressure tokens emitted by runtime
Fallback selection chooses compatible variant with highest compatibility score and within cost tier constraints, documented in policy logs
Geo-failover triggers route requests to next-priority region within 2s when healthy instance count falls below configured threshold
Auto-rollback fires only when both quality regression >= 5% on golden prompt set AND 95th percentile token latency increases > 2x baseline for 5 minutes
End-to-end smoke tests (local + staging) demonstrate shadow->canary->rollout flow with simulated region outage and tier saturation
implementation_steps: Design admission control API and policy schema (routing-policy compiler changes) — spec PR in docs/confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/rl/deploy-admission-spec
Prototype compatibility scorer in runtime (lightweight op/shape checks + fingerprinting) — branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feature/compat-scorer
Add capacity bucketing and backpressure token generator to scheduler service
Wire admission check into canary controller and rollout service; implement soft-throttle state machine
Implement cross-region failover priority list and graceful draining logic
Add auto-rollback evaluator that consumes QA eval signals and runtime SLO metrics (Prometheus and tracing)
Create end-to-end integration tests and chaos tests (region simulate down, burst traffic)
technical_notes: Compatibility scoring uses a weighted combination of op-compat (0/1 per op), response-shape similarity (cosine on flattened proto), and model metadata version tags; weights configurable via policy

Admission bucketing estimates token-rate capacity per GPU using 95th percentile throughput samples from the runtime and a safety margin; buckets are soft (can borrow capacity from adjacent buckets with a cost multiplier)
Backpressure tokens are issued as short-lived leases (TTL 10s) with a token count proportional to headroom; controllers stop ramping when tokens exhausted

Fallback selection prefers same-architecture quantized variant if within cost tier, otherwise next-highest compatibility score in same region; cross-region fallback only used when local capacity < configured minimum
Auto-rollback requires an ensemble signal: at least one quality monitor (eval set or user-feedback alert) AND an infra SLO breach; both thresholds are configurable per-project
Logging: each admission decision emits a decision record with reasons, compatibility score, capacity snapshot, and token counts for audit and post-mortem
testing_plan: Unit tests for compatibility scorer with synthetic model metadata and response shapes
Load tests: synthetic token streams to validate bucketing and backpressure behavior
Chaos tests in staging: kill region instances and verify geo-failover within 2s and no request loss
Regression tests for auto-rollback: inject quality regression and latency spike and assert rollback occurs only when both signals present
Observability tests: ensure decision records surface in console rollout dashboard and trace links to PRs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): internal traffic only, 1% global, observe for 24h; disable auto-rollback to avoid churn
Phase 1 (expanded canary): 5% global, enable backpressure tokens, monitor capacity and compatibility logs
Phase 2 (regional): enable per-region bucketing, simulate regional load to validate soft-throttle and cross-region fallback
Phase 3 (production): gradual full rollout with auto-rollback enabled and monitoring alerts configured
metrics: Median and 95th percentile request queueing delay at admission
Fallback activation count and latency delta when fallback used
Auto-rollback frequency and root-cause signals (quality vs infra)
